topics.title: Set 2 Speed Sounds: ay ee igh ow oo ar or air ir ou oy
topics.intro: Every Speed Sound has a phrase to help you remember it: ay, may I play! ee, what can you see! Say the phrase, then find the sound in a word.
topics.teach: Teach me the phrase for “igh” and two words with that sound.
topics.talk: These follow the Read Write Inc. Speed Sounds many schools use. Ask {him} to say the phrase for each sound, and to spot the sounds in a book.

topics.title: Set 3 Speed Sounds 1: ea oi a-e i-e o-e u-e aw are ur er
topics.intro: Set 3 sounds are new ways to write sounds you know. a-e is a split special friend: make a cake! The e at the end makes the a say its name.
topics.teach: Explain how “slid” changes when you add an e at the end.
topics.talk: These follow the Read Write Inc. Speed Sounds many schools use. Ask {him} for the phrase for a-e, i-e and o-e, and to read slid/slide, hop/hope.

topics.title: Set 3 Speed Sounds 2: ow ai oa ew ire ear ure tion cious e
topics.intro: More Set 3 sounds: brown cow, snail in the rain, goat in a boat. Some sounds have two spellings: ay at the end of a word (play), ai in the middle (rain).
topics.teach: Explain when to use “ay” and when to use “ai”.
topics.talk: These follow the Read Write Inc. Speed Sounds many schools use. Ask {him} to write day and rain and explain the spelling choice.

topics.title: Fred Talk and Fred Fingers
topics.intro: Fred Talk means saying the sounds in a word, then pushing them together: sh-i-p, ship! Fred Fingers means holding up one finger for each sound. Special friends like sh and igh are one sound, so they get one finger.
topics.teach: Fred Talk “night” for me, and tell me how many sounds it has.
topics.talk: These follow the Read Write Inc. Speed Sounds many schools use. Say a word in Fred Talk (ch-ai-n) and ask {him} to say the word.

topics.title: Red words and green words
topics.intro: Green words can be read by Fred Talking them. Red words are tricky: they don’t sound the way they look, so “you can’t Fred a red”. We learn red words by heart.
topics.teach: Explain why “said” is a red word.
topics.talk: These follow the Read Write Inc. Speed Sounds many schools use. Write five red words on sticky notes around the house; {she} reads each one as {she} passes.

topics.title: Alien words
topics.intro: Alien words are made-up words. They aren’t real, so you can’t guess them: you have to Fred Talk them. Ready for some alien names?
topics.teach: Fred Talk the alien word “zort”. Which Speed Sound is in it?
topics.talk: The Year 1 phonics check uses alien words, and they are still great practice: make up alien names together and read them.
